Pinned-release triage: karajan-code 4.49.3
Judgement: BENIGN for the archive, knip 6.41.0, karajan-core 1.5.0,
board.js and install-binary.sh. The LPM version-specific claim is unsupported
by the inspected bytes; its webpage was inaccessible during this review.

The postinstall entrypoint writes local Claude/Codex MCP registrations. It
neither downloads code nor sends secrets. The board launcher starts a logged,
PID-tracked server on loopback by default. Remote board access uses a generated
bearer token. Telemetry requires config.telemetry === true. Cloud embeddings
send caller-supplied text to configured provider APIs, with the supplied API
key used for authorization. The bootstrap downloads official Node or project
release assets, verifies SHA-256 checksums, installs user-local executables,
and optionally removes the standalone executable's quarantine attribute.

Knip analyzes project imports, exports and dependency use; its Hardhat plugin
names config files rather than accessing mnemonic material. Its git helpers
query repository metadata. Karajan Core implements local SQLite/RAG stores,
process timeout/streaming helpers and configured embedding adapters. Its
archive matches both supplied SHA-1 and SHA-512 pins. Vendored WASM files are
tree-sitter grammars; Rizin inspection showed parser/memory interfaces rather
than executable download/network capabilities. binwalk was not on PATH.

Corrections preserve neutral observations and remove inferred intent:
- daemon lifecycle and announcement observations leave the dropper namespace;
- process-tree references leave debugger detection;
- enabledPlugins assignments leave startup injection;
- agent instruction surfaces and Git branch cleanup leave supply-chain intent;
- verbatim output requests leave reasoning-extraction evasion;
- Hardhat config is removed from the mnemonic-file matcher; actual mnemonic
  names use neutral filename traits consumed by the existing source cluster;
- comments no longer trigger dynamic imports or destruction wording;
- erased TypeScript import types are excluded, with chained runtime imports
  retained;
- governance wording is distinguished from a directed no-escape threat;
- a generic TimeoutError class and run.ts reference no longer identify
  p-timeout or Changesets Action;
- a monorepo sibling repository does not identify Karajan Code itself;
- Xenova dynamic imports are module loads rather than importer identity.

Exact YAML consumers were updated. Ancestor selectors of the affected leaves
were reviewed: neutral facts no longer supply objective/family directory
membership. No new broad benign-name suppression was introduced. New files
use existing admitted leaves. Fifteen positive/near-miss controls are recorded in
cases.json. Their assertions were checked against a single batch Cleave scan.
All five Atomscan input reports have zero hostile and zero suspicious traits.
Judgement markers live beside the original archive, its archive-view names,
the extracted highlighted sources, and the dependency tarballs under scratch.
